correctness.rationale: The change of variables to three independent signs is bijective and converts the chaos to a Walsh polynomial with only degrees one and two. Orthogonality gives zero sum on each parity class. For any real four-vector of sum zero, splitting positive and negative parts proves \(\ell_1\ge\sqrt2\,\ell_2\) with exact equality characterization. Applying this on both parity classes with the exact eight-point normalization yields \(\|h\|_2\le2\|h\|_1\). Equality forces one parity class to vanish and the other to have exactly two opposite nonzero values; cube symmetries give precisely the product family. The \(n=2\) and \(n=3\) constants follow by the same argument.

value.rationale: The four-variable case is the minimal dimension capable of realizing the standard sharpness witness for the open degree-two moment-comparison conjecture. Establishing the exact constant there, classifying all equality cases, and proving the strict lower-dimensional profile \(1,\sqrt2,2\) identifies a natural boundary of the open problem rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
